# Windsurf Pricing: Current Plans and Legacy Credits

Updated October 28, 2026

Windsurf's pricing URL now redirects to Devin's pricing page. As checked October 28, 2026, it lists Free at $0, Pro at $20 per month and Max at $200 per month. Teams has an $80 monthly minimum with $40 full seats, explained in the billing documentation. Enterprise pricing requires a quote. Older references to $15 Pro and a universal 500-credit allowance should not be used for a new purchase.

This is a documentation-based buying guide, not a hands-on performance review. Compare plans by who needs editor access, how often they use agents, what happens after included usage, and which administrative controls the organization requires. A higher subscription price does not establish better code quality.

## Our data: six subscription budget scenarios

We calculated two individual-plan annualized costs and four team seat scenarios from the current published monthly prices. The inputs, formulas and exclusions are below. These are planning examples, not customer invoices. AI assisted the research and drafting; PE Collective is responsible for the editorial analysis.

[Current plans](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#plans) · [Free versus Pro](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#free) · [Quotas and credits](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#usage) · [Team budget](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#teams) · [Legacy plans](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#legacy) · [Buying checklist](https://pecollective.com/tools/windsurf-pricing/#decision)

## Windsurf pricing plans and the current Devin destination

| Plan | Published monthly price | Decision to make |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0  | Can you evaluate the workflow within limited agent usage? |
| Pro | $20 | Does regular individual work fit the included usage? |
| Max | $200 | Does sustained individual use justify the larger allowance? |
| Teams | $80 minimum; $40 per full seat | Who needs a full desktop seat versus occasional shared usage? |
| Enterprise | Custom | Which contractual, deployment and administration requirements need a quote? |

Sources: [current pricing](https://devin.ai/pricing) and [self-serve billing documentation](https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve). The marketing page's team headline can read like a base fee plus seats; the detailed billing table instead describes an $80 minimum satisfied by seats and credits. The examples here follow that explicit billing table. Confirm the checkout total for your account before buying.

The product name matters when comparing an old invoice with a new subscription. Follow the plan destination from your account and record its effective date. A search result using “Windsurf Pro” may describe a historical offer, an existing customer's terms, or the current individual product. Those cases can have different allowances even when the monthly charge looks similar.

Keep the plan price separate from your agent budget. Subscription cost, included allowance, purchased extra usage and taxes are different lines in the calculation. An apparently cheap seat can still be expensive for a team that runs many long sessions, while a higher seat price may cover work that otherwise incurs usage charges.

## Is Windsurf free, and when does Pro make sense?

The current Free plan includes limited agent use and model availability, plus unlimited inline edits and Tab completions according to the pricing page. That makes it suitable for examining the editor workflow before choosing a paid plan. “Unlimited completions” should not be read as unlimited agent work; the two interactions have different limits.

Use a bounded evaluation task from your normal work. For example, ask the tool to explain a small module, change a validation rule, and show the relevant tests. Inspect the diff and run the same checks you would require from a colleague. Record where you needed to correct context, reject edits or explain repository conventions.

Free is a reasonable starting point when you are learning the interface or doing occasional changes. It is a weaker planning assumption for a deadline-driven project that depends on repeated agent sessions. Decide beforehand what you will do if you reach a limit: finish manually, wait for the reset, or make an approved purchase.

Pro is the first paid individual option in the current lineup. Its role is regular single-person usage. Before upgrading, identify the problem you want the subscription to solve. Running out of agent allowance is different from using the wrong model, missing project context or asking for changes the repository cannot support.

A subscription cannot repair an incomplete task description. Give the agent the failing behavior, expected outcome, relevant files and verification command. Smaller, well-scoped requests are easier to assess, and they also make it possible to compare how much usage a task consumes. A long conversation full of unrelated material makes that comparison harder.

## How quotas and extra usage work

The [billing documentation](https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve) describes daily and weekly allowances for Pro and full team seats; Max has a larger weekly allowance without a daily cap. Purchased on-demand credits can fund additional usage and roll forward. Flex seats draw from shared team credits and do not include Desktop access. These are current billing categories, distinct from old Windsurf prompt-credit tables.

Do not convert a quota into an invented number of tasks. A short explanation and a multi-step repository change can consume different amounts of work. The model, input context, generated output and tool activity affect consumption. A fixed “requests per month” comparison would hide those differences unless the provider defines the same unit for every request.

For your own estimate, record three task types: a small edit, a routine feature and a difficult debugging session. Track the account's usage movement around each task. Use several examples per type before assigning a budget. This is a proposed measurement method, not a claim that PE Collective observed those costs.

Keep reset allowance and purchased balance in separate columns. A reset can replenish included capacity without refunding an already purchased credit. A remaining balance can also outlive the particular project that caused the purchase. That distinction matters when comparing a one-month experiment with a subscription your team expects to keep for a year.

[![まさお@未経験からプロまでAI活用](https://assets.st-note.com/production/uploads/images/167321889/profile_253b11b07efa249024f94534e1940ab5.jpg?width=60)](https://note.com/masa_wunder)

**Major overhaul of the credit system with "Pricing v2"**

*   **Complete abolition of Flow Action credits**  
    Previously, additional credits were consumed based on "internal file reading/writing and the number of steps by the agent (Cascade Agent)." However, this has been abolished since "Pricing v2," and it has been unified into **"1 prompt = 1 credit" regardless of how much processing happens in the background**.
    
*   **Consolidated into three plans: Personal Pro, Teams, and Enterprise**  
    Monthly fees and prompt limits have been clarified. The personal **Pro** plan is **$15/month for 500 prompts**, the **Teams** plan is **$30/seat for 500 prompts**, and the large-scale **Enterprise** plan is **$60/seat for 1,000 prompts**.
    
*   **Additional credits are standardized as "Flex credits" with no expiration**  
    Once you use up your prompts, you can purchase additional capacity such as **$10 for 250 credits** (for Pro/Teams). Unused portions carry over to the following months.
    
*   **"Grandfather" migration for existing users**  
    Users currently under old plans can maintain their old terms for a certain period. For example, users of the old Pro plan (500 prompts + 1,500 Flows) are being automatically migrated to the new plan while receiving measures such as bonuses added to their remaining points.
    

**In short**:  
The previously confusing dual calculation of "prompt count + Flow Action" has been eliminated, and billing has been unified simply to "prompts only," making it clear **"how much it costs based on usage"**. On the other hand, for users who primarily used a high number of prompts, this may feel like a de facto price increase.

* * *

## Windsurf's current market position

Windsurf is an AI code assistance platform that has grown rapidly, exceeding 1 million users in about a year and a half and reaching over 1,500 corporate clients.  
[Furthermore, its ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) has reached approximately $40 million, and it is attracting significant market attention, with reports that **OpenAI is in acquisition talks for around $3 billion**.](https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/16/openai-is-reportedly-in-talks-to-buy-windsurf-for-3b-with-news-expected-later-this-week/?utm_source=chatgpt.com&guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly9jaGF0Z3B0LmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAH2m0Qr0AW5HHzkJuQEU87iUDYtOavc5dB4VdaBLyPoW4M_Amngh8ayUjVBf79rAuclJtie2YPXK3Cq0nPHV1F6h95FYr2mnow9djLhiCA1jA_iQxLHwwayOIlji36pDCrHwSyS11UYE32CAlRp0PUZK-NJnme9WvT0-ZPc0NK0R)

*   **Over $200 million in total funding**  
    Since its inception, the company has leveraged its strengths in GPU infrastructure and has actively addressed enterprise-grade self-hosting and security requirements (such as obtaining SOC 2 certification) to capture corporate users.
    
*   **Presence as an "AI-native IDE"**  
    Its design is deeply integrated into development tools, such as the built-in agent (Cascade Agent) being able to automate command sequences. It highlights functionality that sets it apart from other editor extensions and is leading the market.
    

> \[Author's Thoughts\]  
> There is speculation that this plan revision aims to clarify the company's valuation in light of reports regarding acquisition negotiations by OpenAI.  
> [https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43755321](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43755321)

## What is Windsurf in the first place?

Windsurf (formerly Codeium) is an **Integrated Development Environment (IDE) specialized for AI-powered coding assistance** and a service that provides multiple plugins. It has a dedicated editor called "Windsurf Editor" for Mac/Windows/Linux, and also officially supports **over 20 plugins** including VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim, Emacs, Xcode, and Jupyter.

* * *

## What is the difference between Cursor and Windsurf?

Comparing it with "Cursor (The AI Code Editor)," which has been gaining attention recently, the differences are as follows:

*   While Windsurf requires credit-based billing, the AI agent inside, Cascade, is extremely capable (based on my personal experience). They frequently mention their focus on memory systems. They introduce unique improvements to the development experience.
    
*   Cursor can be used for a flat fee if you can tolerate slow requests, its UI/UX has improved, and I consider it an all-purpose AI development editor that generally has everything else available.
    

That is my impression.

* * *

## Differences between Windsurf, Devin, ClaudeCode, and Cline (RooCode)

In addition to Windsurf and Cursor, competing services like "Devin" and "Cline (VS Code extension)" have recently emerged.

*   Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc., are positioned as basic AI development editors.
    
*   Devin is positioned to unleash the power of those AI development editors.
    
*   ClaudeCode and Codex are positioned to deploy Devin locally.
    

That is how I perceive them.

> I use Cursor, Windsurf, RooCode, Copilot, and AugmentCode in combination, but if I could only choose one from the editors above, assuming I could use Devin and ClaudeCode, I would choose Windsurf (at present). The reason is that I believe the remaining value of these AI development editors compared to other development agents lies in partial optimization tasks, so considering Windsurf's excellent UX, agent quality, and functional balance, I want to recommend it. In that sense, Cursor is my second recommendation (due to its versatility). It is true that all of them are excellent, as Roo, Copilot, and Augment each have their own strengths in agent performance and potential.

# Windsurf

Coding

Codeium's agentic IDE — Cascade + multi-file editing.

[Visit Windsurf](https://codeium.com/windsurf)

## How to use Windsurf

Install the desktop editor or plugin and open your project, then use Cascade to give the agent a task and it plans and edits across files. Rely on unlimited tab completion for line-level work and switch models as needed. Watch daily and weekly quotas rather than a monthly credit pool.

## Best for

Agentic multi-file edits through the Cascade agent. Fast inference with its proprietary model. Unlimited tab autocomplete on every plan, including free.

## How it behaves

A desktop editor that in 2026 dropped credits for a daily and weekly quota model. It runs a fast proprietary model plus third-party frontier models, with an agent, code maps, and background sessions, and is now part of Cognition.

## Tips

Lean on unlimited tab completion, it is free on every plan. Give Cascade whole tasks, not just single edits. Track your daily and weekly quotas.

## Pricing

Free tier with light quotas and unlimited tab completion. Pro is $20/mo, Max is $200/mo for the highest quotas, and Teams is $40 per user.
